audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph David coronation, Jerusalem conquest, and warrior roster, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 5 and 23 for coronation consensus, shepherd-ruler language, Jebusite inhabitants, conquest incentive, Joab's elevation, warrior body counts, food-land defense, Bethlehem water risk, Moabite and Egyptian killings, body-size language, foreign warriors, and Uriah.

verses.restored: All Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, Look, we are your bone and flesh.

familiar.text: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.

modern.text: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, “Here we are, your own flesh and blood.

original.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֧וּ כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל דָּוִ֖יד חֶבְר֣וֹנָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֛ה עַצְמְךָ֥ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ֖ אֲנָֽחְנוּ

verses.restored: In past, even when Saul was king, you were one leading Israel out and in; YHWH your Divine said, You shall shepherd my people Israel and be ruler over my people Israel.

familiar.text: And moreover in time past, even when Saul was king, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD thy God said unto thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be ruler over my people Israel.

modern.text: Even in times past, while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. And the LORD your God said, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be ruler over them.’”

original.text: גַּם תְּמ֣וֹל גַּם שִׁלְשׁ֗וֹם גַּ֚ם בִּהְי֣וֹת שָׁא֣וּל מֶ֔לֶךְ אַתָּ֛ה הַמּוֹצִ֥יא וְהַמֵּבִ֖יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּאמֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ לְךָ֗ אַתָּ֨ה תִרְעֶ֤ה אֶת עַמִּי֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: All elders of Israel came to king at Hebron; David cut covenant with them there before YHWH, and they anointed David king over Israel according to word of YHWH by Samuel.

familiar.text: Therefore came all the elders of Israel to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD by Samuel.

modern.text: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, where David made a covenant with them before the LORD. And they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD through Samuel. David Conquers Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:6–11)

original.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ כָּל זִקְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶל הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ חֶבְר֔וֹנָה וַיִּכְרֹת֩ לָהֶ֨ם דָּוִ֥יד בְּרִ֛ית בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּמְשְׁח֨וּ אֶת דָּוִ֤יד לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד שְׁמוּאֵֽל

verses.restored: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is Jebus, where Jebusites were inhabitants of land.

familiar.text: And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus; where the Jebusites were, the inhabitants of the land.

modern.text: Then David and all the Israelites marched to Jerusalem (that is, Jebus), where the Jebusites inhabited the land.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ דָּוִ֧יד וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הִ֣יא יְב֑וּס וְשָׁם֙ הַיְבוּסִ֔י יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Inhabitants of Jebus said to David, You shall not come here. Yet David captured stronghold of Zion, which became city of David.

familiar.text: And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, Thou shalt not come hither. Nevertheless David took the castle of Zion, which is the city of David.

modern.text: The people of Jebus said to David, “You will never get in here.” Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י יְבוּס֙ לְדָוִ֔יד לֹ֥א תָב֖וֹא הֵ֑נָּה וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד דָּוִיד֙ אֶת מְצֻדַ֣ת צִיּ֔וֹן הִ֖יא עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד

verses.restored: David said, Whoever strikes Jebusites first shall become chief and commander. Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.

familiar.text: And David said, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain. So Joab the son of Zeruiah went first up, and was chief.

modern.text: Now David had said, “Whoever is the first to strike down a Jebusite will become chief commander.” And Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became the chief.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔יד כָּל מַכֵּ֤ה יְבוּסִי֙ בָּרִ֣אשׁוֹנָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֥ה לְרֹ֖אשׁ וּלְשָׂ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָ֛ה יוֹאָ֥ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֖ה וַיְהִ֥י לְרֹֽאשׁ

verses.restored: David lived in stronghold; therefore they called it city of David.

familiar.text: And David dwelt in the castle; therefore they called it the city of David.

modern.text: So David took up residence in the fortress; that is why it was called the City of David.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב דָּוִ֖יד בַּמְצָ֑ד עַל כֵּ֥ן קָרְאוּ ל֖וֹ עִ֥יר דָּוִֽיד

verses.restored: He built city around, from Millo and around; Joab repaired/restored rest of city.

familiar.text: And he built the city round about, even from Millo round about: and Joab repaired the rest of the city.

modern.text: He built up the city around it, from the supporting terraces to the surrounding wall, while Joab restored the rest of the city.

original.text: וַיִּ֤בֶן הָעִיר֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב מִן הַמִּלּ֖וֹא וְעַד הַסָּבִ֑יב וְיוֹאָ֕ב יְחַיֶּ֖ה אֶת שְׁאָ֥ר הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: David grew greater and greater, for YHWH of armies was with him, in narrator's theology.

familiar.text: So David waxed greater and greater: for the LORD of hosts was with him.

modern.text: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD of Hosts was with him. David’s Mighty Men (2 Samuel 23:8–39)

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖יד הָל֣וֹךְ וְגָד֑וֹל וַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: These were heads of David's mighty warriors, who strengthened themselves with him in kingdom, with all Israel, to make him king according to word of YHWH concerning Israel.

familiar.text: These also are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who strengthened themselves with him in his kingdom, and with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

modern.text: Now these were the chiefs of David’s mighty men, who, together with all Israel, bolstered and strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

original.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֤י הַגִּבּוֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֔יד הַמִּתְחַזְּקִ֨ים עִמּ֧וֹ בְמַלְכוּת֛וֹ עִם כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִיכ֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: This is number/list of David's mighty warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of thirty/three; he lifted spear against three hundred slain at one time.

familiar.text: And this is the number of the mighty men whom David had; Jashobeam, an Hachmonite, the chief of the captains: he lifted up his spear against three hundred slain by him at one time.

modern.text: This is the list of David’s mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni was chief of the officers; he wielded his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed at one time.

original.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה מִסְפַּ֥ר הַגִּבֹּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑יד יָשָׁבְעָ֣ם בֶּן חַכְמוֹנִ֗י רֹ֚אשׁ השלושים הֽוּא עוֹרֵ֧ר אֶת חֲנִית֛וֹ עַל שְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֥וֹת חָלָ֖ל בְּפַ֥עַם אֶחָֽת

verses.restored: After him Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of three mighty warriors.

familiar.text: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighties.

modern.text: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.

original.text: וְאַחֲרָ֛יו אֶלְעָזָ֥ר בֶּן דּוֹד֖וֹ הָאֲחוֹחִ֑י ה֖וּא בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים

verses.restored: He was with David at Pas-dammim when Philistines gathered for battle, where a parcel of land was full of barley; people fled before Philistines.

familiar.text: He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where was a parcel of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.

modern.text: He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. At the place with a field full of barley, the troops fled from the Philistines.

original.text: הֽוּא הָיָ֨ה עִם דָּוִ֜יד בַּפַּ֣ס דַּמִּ֗ים וְהַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ נֶאֱסְפוּ שָׁ֣ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֛י חֶלְקַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מְלֵאָ֣ה שְׂעוֹרִ֑ים וְהָעָ֥ם נָ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: They stood in middle of parcel, rescued it, and struck Philistines; YHWH saved by great deliverance, in narrator's interpretation.

familiar.text: And they set themselves in the midst of that parcel, and delivered it, and slew the Philistines; and the LORD saved them by a great deliverance.

modern.text: But Eleazar and David stationed themselves in the middle of the field and defended it. They struck down the Philistines, and the LORD brought about a great victory.

original.text: וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֤וּ בְתוֹךְ הַחֶלְקָה֙ וַיַּצִּיל֔וּהָ וַיַּכּ֖וּ אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיּ֥וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֖ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: Three of thirty chiefs went down to rock to David at cave of Adullam while Philistine camp was in valley of Rephaim.

familiar.text: Now three of the thirty captains went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the host of the Philistines encamped in the valley of Rephaim.

modern.text: Three of the thirty chief men went down to David, to the rock at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

original.text: וַיֵּרְד֡וּ שְֽׁלוֹשָׁה֩ מִן הַשְּׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים רֹ֤אשׁ עַל הַצֻּר֙ אֶל דָּוִ֔יד אֶל מְעָרַ֖ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֹנָ֖ה בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים

verses.restored: David was in stronghold, and Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.

familiar.text: And David was then in the hold, and the Philistines’ garrison was then at Bethlehem.

modern.text: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.

original.text: וְדָוִ֖יד אָ֣ז בַּמְּצוּדָ֑ה וּנְצִ֣יב פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אָ֖ז בְּבֵ֥ית לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: David longed and said, Who will give me water to drink from well of Bethlehem by gate?

familiar.text: And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Bethlehem, that is at the gate!

modern.text: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”

original.text: ויתאו דָּוִ֖יד וַיֹּאמַ֑ר מִ֚י יַשְׁקֵ֣נִי מַ֔יִם מִבּ֥וֹר בֵּֽית לֶ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁעַר

verses.restored: The three broke through Philistine camp, drew water from well of Bethlehem by gate, carried and brought it to David. He would not drink it but poured it out to YHWH.

familiar.text: And the three brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but David would not drink of it, but poured it out to the LORD,

modern.text: So the Three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,

original.text: וַיִּבְקְע֨וּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁ֜ה בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ מַ֨יִם֙ מִבּ֤וֹר בֵּֽית לֶ֨חֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֶל דָּוִ֑יד וְלֹֽא אָבָ֤ה דָוִיד֙ לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֔ם וַיְנַסֵּ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: He said, Far be it from me before my Divine to do this. Shall I drink blood/lives of these men who went at risk of their lives? At risk of lives they brought it. He would not drink. These things the three mighty warriors did.

familiar.text: And said, My God forbid it me, that I should do this thing: shall I drink the blood of these men that have put their lives in jeopardy? for with the jeopardy of their lives they brought it. Therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mightiest.

modern.text: saying, “Far be it from me, my God, to do this! How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?” Because they had brought it at the risk of their lives, David refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

original.text: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר חָלִילָה֩ לִּ֨י מֵאֱלֹהַ֜י מֵעֲשׂ֣וֹת זֹ֗את הֲדַ֣ם הָאֲנָשִׁים֩ הָאֵ֨לֶּה אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה בְנַפְשׁוֹתָם֙ כִּ֣י בְנַפְשׁוֹתָ֣ם הֱבִיא֔וּם וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֑ם אֵ֣לֶּה עָשׂ֔וּ שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת הַגִּבּוֹרִֽים

verses.restored: Abishai brother of Joab was chief of three; he lifted spear against three hundred and killed them and had a name among three.

familiar.text: And Abishai the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three: for lifting up his spear against three hundred, he slew them, and had a name among the three.

modern.text: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.

original.text: וְאַבְשַׁ֣י אֲחִֽי יוֹאָ֗ב ה֤וּא הָיָה֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֔ה וְהוּא֙ עוֹרֵ֣ר אֶת חֲנִית֔וֹ עַל שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חָלָ֑ל ולא שֵׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁלוֹשָֽׁה

verses.restored: Among second three he was honored above two and became their commander, but did not attain first three.

familiar.text: Of the three, he was more honourable than the two; for he was their captain: howbeit he attained not to the first three.

modern.text: He was doubly honored above the Three, and he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.

original.text: מִן הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֤ה בַשְּׁנַ֨יִם֙ נִכְבָּ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וְעַד הַשְּׁלוֹשָׁ֖ה לֹֽא בָֽא

verses.restored: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, did many acts; he struck two sons/warriors of Ariel of Moab and went down and struck a lion in pit on snowy day.

familiar.text: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who had done many acts; he slew two lionlike men of Moab: also he went down and slew a lion in a pit in a snowy day.

modern.text: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

original.text: בְּנָיָ֨ה בֶן יְהוֹיָדָ֧ע בֶּן אִֽישׁ חַ֛יִל רַב פְּעָלִ֖ים מִֽן קַבְצְאֵ֑ל ה֣וּא הִכָּ֗ה אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י אֲרִיאֵל֙ מוֹאָ֔ב וְ֠הוּא יָרַ֞ד וְהִכָּ֧ה אֶֽת הָאֲרִ֛י בְּת֥וֹךְ הַבּ֖וֹר בְּי֥וֹם הַשָּֽׁלֶג

verses.restored: He struck an Egyptian man of great stature, five cubits; in Egyptian's hand was spear like weaver's beam. He went down with staff, seized spear from Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.

familiar.text: And he slew an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high; and in the Egyptian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and slew him with his own spear.

modern.text: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man five cubits tall. Although the Egyptian had a spear like a weaver’s beam in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.

original.text: וְהֽוּא הִכָּה֩ אֶת הָאִ֨ישׁ הַמִּצְרִ֜י אִ֥ישׁ מִדָּ֣ה חָמֵ֣שׁ בָּאַמָּ֗ה וּבְיַ֨ד הַמִּצְרִ֤י חֲנִית֙ כִּמְנ֣וֹר אֹרְגִ֔ים וַיֵּ֥רֶד אֵלָ֖יו בַּשָּׁ֑בֶט וַיִּגְזֹ֤ל אֶֽת הַחֲנִית֙ מִיַּ֣ד הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַיַּהַרְגֵ֖הוּ בַּחֲנִיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did and had a name among three mighty warriors.

familiar.text: These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had the name among the three mighties.

modern.text: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name alongside the three mighty men.

original.text: אֵ֣לֶּה עָשָׂ֔ה בְּנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וְלוֹ שֵׁ֖ם בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה הַגִּבֹּרִֽים

verses.restored: He was honored among thirty but did not attain three; David placed him over bodyguard.

translation_notes: The phrase 'all Israel' expresses the Chronicler's idealized unity and should not erase civil war, Saul loyalists, women, civilians, or dissenting communities.
Jerusalem is an inhabited Jebusite city taken by conquest; renaming it the city of David does not erase prior residents.
David's reward for the first attacker elevates Joab through conquest and incentivizes lethal competition.
Warrior body counts are heroic rhetoric, not models of masculinity or sanctity.
The barley-field defense concerns food and livelihood, but Philistine deaths remain human deaths.
David's casual longing prompts subordinates to risk their lives. Pouring out the water recognizes the cost but does not erase leader responsibility for requests made under unequal power.
Moabite and Egyptian opponents may not be racialized, animalized, or treated as spiritually inferior.
Great stature and unusual bodies are not monstrosity, disability, or proof of threat.
The roster includes Ammonite, Hittite, Moabite, and other foreign-associated warriors, undermining ethnic-purity myths.
Uriah the Hittite's name at verse 41 must recall David's abuse of Bathsheba and command murder; warrior honor cannot bury royal guilt.
safety_note: Do not turn David's coronation into leader cult, Jerusalem's capture into modern conquest entitlement, body counts into masculinity, or foreign opponents into racial enemies. Keep Jebusite residents, risked subordinates, killed opponents, and Uriah's betrayal visible.
